title: FineRMoE: Dimension Expansion for Finer-Grained Expert with an Upcycling Approach
claim: A single router jointly steers sparse selection along two dimensions, so experts specialize beyond what single-dimension fine-graining allows.
layout: Left transformer block zooms into right expert diagram, left-to-right, router at bottom
description: The figure shows the FineRMoE architecture. On the left is a transformer block stack with Self-Attention, Add & Norm, a Shared Expert (orange) and Sparse Experts (gray), with a black arrow leading to an expanded view on the right. The expanded view has four rounded boxes, each with a yellow Weighted Sum node over four E blocks. The two middle boxes are active (blue and red) and the two outer boxes are faded (inactive). A Router at the bottom emits bar charts, one per box, and a Sum node joins them. Checkmarks and crosses mark which outputs are kept. The kept outputs feed a Direct Concat block at the top with a blue-to-red gradient. Labels on the right name the Sparse Sum Layer and the Sparse Concatenation Layer. A small weight-matrix sketch at the lower left separates the output and intermediate dimensions. The eye goes first to the colorful central expert boxes and the router.
caption: The proposed FineRMoE (FineR-grained MoE) architecture. The MoE layer is composed of the shared expert and multiple sparse experts, in which fine-grained design is applied to both the intermediate and output dimensions. The forward process of the sparse experts consists of a sparse sum layer and a sparse concatenation layer. A single router with specially designed routing mechanism simultaneously steers the activation in the two sparse layers.
abstract: As revealed by the scaling law of fine-grained MoE, model performance ceases to be improved once the granularity of the intermediate dimension exceeds the optimal threshold, limiting further gains from single-dimension fine-grained design. To address this bottleneck, we propose FineRMoE (FineR-Grained MoE), an architecture that extends fine-grained expert design to both intermediate and output dimensions, aiming to enhance expert specialization beyond the single-dimension limit. We further introduce a bi-level sparse forward computation paradigm and a specialized routing mechanism to govern the activation. In addition, to obviate the prohibitive cost of training FineRMoE from scratch, we devise a generalized upcycling method to build FineRMoE in a cost-effective manner. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superior performance achieved by FineRMoE across ten standard benchmarks. Compared with the strongest baseline, FineRMoE achieves 6 times higher parameter efficiency, 281 times lower prefill latency, and 136 timese higher decoding throughput during inference.
